detailed_review.score_reasoning:
Baseline penalty sums every baseline finding: F1 2 (missing 'What it does today'), F2 2 (missing persona surface), F3 2 (catalog material on a describing page), F4 2 (inline install procedure), F5 1 (forward reference to 'the plan'), F6 1 (status section on a type that forbids one), F7 1 (comma splice in the abstract), F8 0.5 (five programs, four bullets) = 11.5. 10 - 11.5 = -1.5, floored and clamped to 1, so score_before is 1. Open penalty after the run: F1 2 + F2 2 + F3 2 + F4 2 + F6 1 + F9 1 = 10. 10 - 10 = 0, clamped to 1, so score_after is 1 and the delta is 0. That delta is not a claim that nothing improved. Three findings worth 2.5 points were fixed, but the five structural findings alone carry 9 points, which puts both grades on the floor, and F9 (found on regrade, owned by T16) adds a tenth. The score is a statement about the page's shape: wiki/clients/macos.md declares type platform-overview and is missing two of the six sections that type requires, while carrying two blocks the type explicitly sends elsewhere. No amount of sentence-level correction moves it off the floor, and the corrections T4 was dispatched to make were the right corrections on a page that needs a restructure.

On scope discipline: the size figures were not touched and were not re-filed. crates/hearth-probe/src/lib.rs:26-34 and desktop-client/src/lib/probe.ts:158-164 divide by 1,073,741,824 and label the result GB, and the research artifact reproduces 3.77, 7.14, 4.53 and 8.56 from the dictionary constants. The figure at line 42 and the plan totals at 103-105 are what the installer prints, and nothing in this run changed a digit.

On the judgement the dispatch asked me to test, whether qualifying only the four-item list leaves a reader misled about the free-disk figure at line 42: the author's call holds. Line 42 does not report a download. It reports how much free disk Hearth requires, and it says in the same breath that Hearth checks that space before it starts and warns if it is missing. That number is disk_required from crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:237, the two-item total plus a fifth, which is precisely the threshold the installer enforces, so a reader who budgets from line 42 is budgeting against the check they will actually face. Qualifying it would need a magnitude no source supplies: the omitted engine and Python runtime are 36,326,051 bytes on macOS, but the voice environment's pip installs at crates/hearth-probe/dictionary.yaml:59-67 carry no recorded size anywhere, so the page cannot say whether the plan's one-fifth headroom (roughly 810 MB on the 8 GB tier) absorbs them. A bare warning with no number would leave a reader worse off than the accurate figure. The residual risk is real but it is a product question, not a page defect: if the pip installs ever exceed the headroom, an install can pass the check and still run out of disk. That belongs in a source task against the planner, not in a sentence on this page, and the author already recorded it in unresolved[]. No finding filed.

On the tracker citation the research stage corrected: I confirm it independently. wiki/page-types.md:246-248 forbids a dated status log, and the bullet T4 removed carried no date, so that citation did not reach it. The rule that reached it is :239 read with :264. What :246-248 does reach is still on the page, at lines 124-125, and it is F6.

The linter could not be run in this session (no execution tool). Nothing in found[] is a linter finding, and two items in its territory are named in tooling_note so they read as excluded rather than missed.
detailed_review.what_worked: F5 was the finding worth this run's cost. The author stage copied two qualifying sentences verbatim from wiki/installing.md:109-111, which is exactly right as prose and wrong as placement: on that page the plan and its figure share one section, and on this page they are 40 lines and two sections apart, so the correction opened by referring to 'the plan' before the reader had met it and to 'them' across a paragraph break. The qualifier now introduces the plan in its own paragraph and names 'those four', so the correction lands where the reader can use it, and it no longer depends on a section that tracker row T6 is about to delete. F7 removed a comma splice from the first sentence a reader meets about the product. F8 reconciled 'five local programs' with a list of four bullets, so a reader checking what runs on their machine can count it. All three fixes preserved every figure, link, port, path and UI string on the page.
detailed_review.what_holds_score_down:
Five structural findings and one regrade finding, all open. The page is not shaped like the type it declares. It has no capability section (F1) and no persona-surface section (F2), which are sections 2 and 3 of the platform-overview spine and the two that wiki/clients/ios.md gets right. It carries an install tree and a port list (F3) that wiki/page-types.md:249-250 sends to a reference page, and a four-step install procedure (F4) that :243-245 sends to the install page and that tracker row T6 already owns. Its limits section (F6) is a status section with a date in it, which is the pattern :246-248 forbids, and it lists one capability among its caveats. F9, found on the regrade read, hands a reader a bare filename at the moment their install has failed.

The page's own abstract is the clearest evidence. Lines 27-29 say 'This page covers what your Mac needs, what the install puts on your disk, and how updates work.' That is an accurate description of what the page delivers, and it is a narrower promise than the type makes. The page is internally consistent and consistent with the wrong shape.
